summary: Abridgment of Chapter II keeping all eight verbatim excerpts and the essential plot beats. These include the park encounter, Whittington's description, the card and appointment, the Paris pensionnat offer, 'both or neither', the spontaneous 'Jane Finn', the truthful bluff, the payment, the clerk Brown's telephone message, and the taxi ending.
acceptable_changes: Compressed the post-office telegram to one sentence. It keeps Tommy's retained pencil and drops the club-subscription remark.
Cut the walk to the end of the street and the choice of stairs over the lift. Both were optional.
Turned the 'father would have a fit' aside and the American-friends link to Madame Colombier's into brief narration.

Removed 'You insist on misjudging me' and joined Whittington's two adjacent snarling lines into one turn, condensing the 'quit fooling' rounds. Kept 'I shouldn't like to contradict you, Mr. Whittington.'
Joined some of Whittington's adjacent lines (overhearing and offering help; duration and conditions) and trimmed minor stage business.
risks: Joining Whittington's lines in the 'quit fooling' passage slightly changes the rhythm of the exchange.
The word count is approximate and was not measured with a tool. It may run somewhat over the 1300-word target because dialogue was preserved.
review_focus: Check that the outer office has no telephone and that the clerk's paper is called a 'Telephone message'.
Check that 'Jane Finn' is presented only as her spontaneous invention.
Check that the merged Whittington turn after 'perhaps my knowledge ends there' reads cleanly.
